All six enumerated cases are present and asserted in test/specled_ex/coverage/paths_test.exs: charlist (:8) and binary (:12) to_binary/1; absolute in-repo -> repo-relative (:21-22); out-of-repo -> nil/[] (:28-29); already-relative unchanged (:35-36); non-binary -> nil/[] (:40-43); unloadable module -> nil/[] under both load? modes (:64-66). `mix test test/specled_ex/coverage/paths_test.exs` = 8 tests, 0 failures.

- (c) FAIL, BLOCKING: the load?: false vs load?: true distinction is NOT pinned. Mutation-verified, not inferred. I built two mutants of module_source/2 in scratchpad — one ignoring load? and always calling Code.ensure_loaded, one ignoring load? and always calling :code.is_loaded — and ran the shipped assertions (paths_test.exs:47-67) verbatim against both with the subject module preloaded exactly as it is in the real run. Both mutants PASS all six module_source/2 assertions. The file therefore cannot go RED if the two branches are unified in either direction. Root cause: both tests pick inputs where the two modes agree by construction — an already-loaded module (:52-53, Paths is loaded because the test module references it) and a nonexistent module (:64-65, both branches fall through to nil). This matters in production: lib/specled_ex/coverage/formatter.ex:260 and lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex:436 deliberately pass false (must not force-load during coverage collection), while lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex:137 and lib/mix/tasks/spec.triangle.ex:453 pass true. Four call sites split on this flag and no test defends the split.
  Correct version: assert the only discriminating input — an in-repo module that is loadable but not currently loaded. I confirmed this state is constructible and gives opposite answers:
      mod = SpecLedEx.Review.CoverageClosure
      :code.purge(mod); :code.delete(mod); :code.purge(mod)
      refute match?({_k, _p}, :code.is_loaded(mod))
      assert Paths.module_source(mod, false) == nil
      refute match?({_k, _p}, :code.is_loaded(mod))   # load?: false must not load
      assert Paths.module_source(mod, true) == "lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex"
  Observed: nil / "lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex". That kills both mutants. The purge/delete mutates VM-global code-server state, so it must live in an async: false module (same rationale already documented at test/specled_ex/realization/binding_test.exs:2). The non-loading assertion is the load-bearing half — it pins that load?: false has no side effect, which is exactly why the formatter passes false.

- (b) SECOND SURVIVING MUTANT (warning): the `root <> "/"` boundary guard in lib/specled_ex/coverage/paths.ex:20 is untested. I ran a mutant that drops it to `String.starts_with?(absolute, root)` against all eight shipped repo_relative/1 + repo_relative_list/1 assertions — all eight survive. The guard is deliberate (a sibling directory whose name prefixes the repo root must not resolve): with root .../specled_ex-coverage-source-resolver, input .../specled_ex-coverage-source-resolver-sibling/lib/foo.ex returns nil on the real impl and leaks the full absolute path on the mutant. Add: `assert Paths.repo_relative(root <> "-sibling/lib/foo.ex") == nil` (root derived via File.cwd!() as at :18). The existing out-of-repo case at :26 uses /tmp/..., which is far outside the root and exercises no boundary.

- (b) minor: :55 and :66 wrap module_source/2 output in repo_relative_list/1 and re-assert what :22, :29 and :43 already cover. Harmless, but not load-bearing — they are composition restatements, not new constraints.

- (d) CWD: no functional break. :18-19 correctly derives root from File.cwd!() rather than hardcoding, and :33 uses a relative path that resolves identically under any cwd. :50 hardcodes the expected repo-relative string, which is safe only because ExUnit runs from the project root — verified passing in the stage worktree. However the module is `async: true` and reads the VM-global cwd (via Paths), and it does not carry the async-safety note this repo requires for exactly this hazard; compare test/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure_test.exs:22-26, which documents that the suite's only File.cd!/1 (test/specled_ex/realization/binding_test.exs:56) lives in an async: false module and ExUnit never overlaps async and sync modules. The reasoning still holds, so this is a convention gap, not a race — but it should be stated, since the load?-discriminating test above will force this module to async: false anyway.

- (e) HYGIENE: clean. No Process.sleep, no spawned or unmanaged processes, no start_supervised needed, no tmp-file writes. The "/tmp/not-in-this-repo/source.ex" at :26 is a pure string input never touched on disk, so there is no shared-tmp collision. async: true (ETC-CORE-001), one describe per public function (ETC-CORE-002), and the self-guarding preconditions at :61-62 are genuinely good — they prove the fixture module really is unloadable instead of trusting the name to be unique.

Verdict: the file is a correct and reasonably thorough pin for to_binary/1, repo_relative/1 and repo_relative_list/1, but it does not do the one job the ticket names as key. As shipped, the four call sites could be silently unified on load? and this suite stays green.
